report_name: Fragmented Federal Rules Divert Resources from Cyber Incident Response

identities.name: Auburn University’s McCrary Institute for Cyber and Critical Infrastructure Security
identities.description: Co-published a report titled "From Fragmentation to Coordination: Operationalizing U.S. Cyber Incident Reporting," which warns that fragmented federal cyber incident reporting rules hinder incident response.

identities.name: U.S. Chamber of Commerce
identities.description: Co-published a report with the McCrary Institute identifying 117 distinct federal reporting regulations and advocating for a streamlined 'report once, use many times' model.

identities.name: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency
identities.description: A U.S. federal agency that is a recipient of cyber incident reports and is recommended by a joint report to manage a single, unified portal for all federal incident reporting.

identities.name: Federal Bureau of Investigation
identities.description: One of the multiple federal agencies to which organizations in critical infrastructure sectors are legally required to report cyber incidents.

identities.name: Government Accountability Office
identities.description: A U.S. government agency whose recent review highlighted the scale of fragmentation in federal cyber incident reporting.

identities.name: Office of the National Cyber Director
identities.description: A U.S. government body recommended to lead the effort to harmonize cyber incident reporting requirements across all federal agencies.

identities.name: Cyber Incident Reporting Council
identities.description: An existing interagency body recommended to be empowered as the primary coordinator for deconflicting federal reporting requirements.

identities.name: U.S. Critical Infrastructure Organizations
identities.description: Private industry organizations within the 16 U.S. critical infrastructure sectors that are negatively impacted by the duplicative and fragmented federal cyber incident reporting requirements.
